meta.heading: Round 9: notes on the Desk, ticket notes, and what the Canvas is
meta.intro: Real screenshots of what's built (sample data), plus the Canvas plan in one picture. Round 8 is in the Archive.

r9-desk.title: Built: notes on the Desk, and a few words on each ticket
body: **Notes on the Desk** (decided in round 4, now built): a Notes card under Done tickets with three tabs. **Jot** keeps a quick thought (Ctrl+Enter); your last few jots sit underneath. **Today** is the day's note; it saves as you type, and picking another day on the ribbon shows that day's note. **Meetings** lists recent meeting notes with a New meeting note button. All of it is in Notes and Find too.

**A few words on each ticket:** every ticket in the Done tickets tray has a box between the ticket and its minutes. Type, then click away or press Enter, and it's saved. Hover a long note to read all of it.

figures.caption: The Desk: entries on the left; Done tickets with notes, then Notes, on the right.
Done tickets: a few words beside each ticket. The third one is being typed.
Notes → **Meetings**: recent meeting notes and New meeting note.

options.why: Say what to change in the note.

questions.legend: Where should Notes sit on the Desk?

options.value: Under the entries on the left

r9-desk.pick: Yes, as shown. Done tickets stays on top because you use it all day.

r9-canvas.title: Decided: the Canvas is the Desk's data, laid out freely
body: The Canvas is not a separate place with separate things in it. It's another way to look at the same entries, tickets and notes as the Desk and the Notes view. Each one is a card. Change a card and the Desk, the Timesheet and Find all see the change.

Everything you do on the Desk works on the Canvas too: Log work, the Done tickets tray and Ctrl+Space capture put new cards on it; double-click a card to open its details; drag a card into a project's area and its project really changes (with Undo). The only new thing the Canvas saves is where you put each card.
On top of that sit the round 8 decisions: stacks, drawers, boards inside boards and the Archive.

figures.caption: The round 8 mockup: the entry **Firewall rule cleanup** and the ticket **VLAN 40 trunk** are the same records you see on the Desk, piled together.
Boards: Meetings, Daily notes and Projects hold the same notes the Notes view lists.

r9-version.title: Releases: take the version from the tag you type
body: The 0.3.0 downloads are named 0.2.0, because the app's own version number wasn't raised. The portable .exe doesn't care, but the Windows installer won't upgrade a 0.2.0 install to a build that also calls itself 0.2.0. Publishing a release also starts the build twice; one copy shows as failed although nothing broke.
The fix: the build reads the version from the tag you type on the Releases page (0.4.0 becomes 0.4.0 everywhere) and runs once per release.
r9-version.pick: Yes. One less thing to remember when you release.
